items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta Interview, 1957-03-28
items.q: I was playing a George Deltzist on Ramport Street, Tom Anderson's son-in-law.

ctx.x: I've seen my hard board right up there. Oh, I've seen it on the biggest one. I want to use that tape, you know, that real, uh, the magnetic tape on.

Keep it in a folder. Those things are hard to find. Yeah. Yeah, Bill George was a very fair fella. Well, he's a guy, he was right in the line. He used to get all those jobs. He's the one sent for, uh, sent for, uh, George Barquet down here. When they went on the Orpins like it. I got an history up there. I believe he used Teppard too, didn't he, on that? That's right. He had an intervention on Carmel. I got there. I got them all up there. And that's why. Did you go to Chicago? For me? Yeah, I went to Chicago in…
For more information, visit www.fema.org Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta Interview, 1957-03-21
items.q: The son-in-law, Tom Anderson's son-in-law, his name was George Delcy. So, it says now we're going to change and want you to go in over and play for my son-in-law.

ctx.x: How old were you by then? About...

...around about 60. And so... the son-in-law. His son-in-law. Open... ...a cabaret... ...on ramparts... ...between the canal... ...and the them. The son-in-law, Tom Anderson's son-in-law, his name was George Delcy. So, it says now we're going to change and want you to go in over and play for my son-in-law. Nice place.
I'd like to ask you a question about the Annex. When you were playing at the Annex, was it only a piano or was it a band there?
